newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore January industrial output drops 7.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore January industrial output drops 7.2 pct.

text.p: A slowdown in most major industries caused a 7.2 percent drop in Singapore's industrial output in January, the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Wednesday.
It was the third consecutive month of year-on-year declines in the city-state's output of manufactured products. December output fell 0.6 percent and November output 4.4 percent.
The EDB said the January drop "was due to a slowdown in most of the major industries, especially in the export-oriented industries whose overall demand remained weak."
Production in the key electronics industry declined 10.9 percent in January, with most segments except disk drives and telecommunication equipment hit by slower orders from overseas, the EDB said.

Singapore's export-oriented economy suffered a slowdown in overall gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1996, when demand fell in the important electronics sector. GDP rose 7.0 percent in 1996, down from 8.8 percent growth in 1995.
The Singapore government has forecast 1997 GDP growth at five to seven percent.
